rv.q: The end result is a richly resonant comedy that reminds us that, while Simon may be pure, he is rarely simple.
Watching DeVito on stage is a privilege, without a doubt, but this isn't comedy at his most deliciously fresh.
The play resonates with wonderful cross-talk and gag-spinning, from the minute DeVito hears his kitchen kettle whistling and picks up the telephone receiver with a bemused “Hello.”

cn.t: DeVito and Griffiths shine in this joyous revival of Simon's 1972 comedy about feuding vaudevillians. DeVito delivers a masterclass performance, while the play proves both profoundly touching and funny in its portrait of old age.
